subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these fourteen third-party GitHub Action revisions for workflows that handle GitHub App keys, registry credentials, release artifacts, security scans, and Codex-agent API keys?
rationale: The patch is a coherent dependency update, but the trust decision is about externally maintained action code executing in privileged workflows; that policy choice cannot be resolved safely from the mechanical SHA diff alone.

options.title: Audit and merge after exact-head runs
options.body: Review the upstream action revisions and merge after rebasing and confirming representative privileged workflow runs on the exact head.

options.title: Hold selected privileged upgrades
options.body: Split out or defer the app-token, Docker credential, and Codex-action revisions if their release changes cannot be accepted yet.

options.title: Close and await a future batch
options.body: Close this automated batch if the workflow owners do not want to accept the expanded action revisions now.

recommendation.title: Audit and merge after exact-head runs
recommendation.body: Review the upstream action revisions and merge after rebasing and confirming representative privileged workflow runs on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for the repository-level workflow and supply-chain decision; the supplied context names no narrower current-main owner.
